title: Redundant Validation inside Barricades
pattern: Routines inside a trusted boundary (private helper methods) repeat parameter sanitization and validation checks on inputs that are structurally guaranteed by the type system or constructor.
why_bad: It duplicates effort (violating DRY), makes invariants less clear, and indicates that developers do not trust their own type system or class boundaries. This lack of trust leads to a spaghetti of redundant verification paths.
detection: Validation conditions checking invariants inside private or internal methods when those invariants are already strictly checked by the public constructor/boundary methods.
fix: Remove the redundant checks. Rely on the constructor validation as the sole source of truth for the type's invariants.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 8.5 ("Relationship Between Barricades and Assertions").
